title: What is an Adjective?
content: An adjective is a word that describes, modifies, or gives more information about a noun or pronoun. Adjectives help the reader visualize, feel, or understand something more precisely.

title: How Adjectives Work
content: Adjectives can appear before a noun ('the red apple', 'a difficult question') or after a linking verb ('she is happy', 'the movie was exciting'). They answer questions like: What kind? Which one? How many? How much?

title: Types of Adjectives
content: Adjectives fall into categories based on what they describe: Opinion (beautiful, difficult), Size (small, large), Age (old, ancient), Shape (round, square), Color (red, green), Origin (Italian, French), Material (wooden, metal), Purpose (racing, sleeping). Each type answers a different question about the noun.

title: The Royal Order of Adjectives
content: When using multiple adjectives, English follows a specific order: Determiner → Quantity → Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Color → Origin → Material → Purpose → Noun. Example: 'My two beautiful small old round green Italian wooden racing chairs.' Breaking this order sounds unnatural to native speakers.

title: Interactive Examples
content: Study these examples: (1) 'The red apple' — red is a color adjective describing the noun apple. (2) 'A difficult question' — difficult is an opinion adjective describing the noun question. (3) 'She is happy' — happy is an emotion adjective describing the pronoun she. (4) 'My two beautiful small old round green Italian wooden racing chairs' — all adjectives follow the Royal Order.

title: Identify the Adjectives
question_text: Identify the adjectives in: 'The tall building is impressive.'
explanation: Both 'tall' (describes the building) and 'impressive' (describes how the building seems) are adjectives.

title: Adjective Order
question_text: Put these adjectives in the correct order: wooden, beautiful, small.
explanation: Opinion (beautiful) comes before Size (small) which comes before Material (wooden).

title: Adjective Order in a Sentence
question_text: Which sentence follows proper adjective order?
explanation: Opinion adjectives (beautiful) come before Material adjectives (wooden).

title: Identify Adjectives in Context
question_text: In 'She bought three expensive red cars', which words are adjectives?
explanation: 'Three' is a number/determiner, 'expensive' is an opinion adjective, 'red' is a color adjective, and 'cars' is a noun.

title: Adjective Type
question_text: What type of adjective is 'ancient' in 'the ancient castle'?
explanation: 'Ancient' describes how old something is, making it an Age adjective.

title: Fill in the Blank: Adjective
question_text: The _____ cat sat on the warm mat.
explanation: We need an adjective to describe the cat. 'Fluffy' describes what the cat looks and feels like.

title: Fill in the Blank: Adjective Order
question_text: She wore a _____ dress to the party.
explanation: Opinion adjectives (beautiful) come before color adjectives (red) in English.

title: Fill in the Blank: Adjective vs Noun
question_text: The movie was very _____.
explanation: 'Exciting' is an adjective that describes what the movie was like. 'Excitement' is a noun.

title: Fill in the Blank: Royal Order
question_text: I bought _____ apples.
explanation: Correct order: Number (three) → Size (small) → Color (red). Remember the Royal Order!

title: Fill in the Blank: Multiple Adjectives
question_text: The _____ building downtown is _____.
explanation: Both blanks need adjectives. 'Old' describes the building, 'impressive' describes how it seems.
